Award/Judgment Factual Position And Pleadings
1.

The present petition was filed on 21.03.2022 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 10,00,000/-
in respect of injuries sustained by Baby Ayushi Rai D/o Sh. Arvind K
umar Rai (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") in a road traffic accident which took place on 05.06.2021 at about 01:30 P.M. at near Baswari Gaon Chauraha, District Sant Kabir Nagar, U.P.

As per this petition, at the relevant date mentioned above, petitioner alongwith her father was waiting for bus/auto to go to Dhanghata Village, suddenly a new TVS Motorcycle(without number plate) came at a very rash and negligent manner from back and hit the petitioner with great force resulting in petitioner falling down on road and receiving multiple injuries all over her body.
She also received fracture injury in left lower limb and kidney injury as blood has come with urine.
After the impact of this accident, the petitioner got unconscious but with the aid of her father and relatives, was given first aid in the nearest Chemist shop situated in PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA
After that her father tried to get her admitted in basti but there is no proper facility available in Basti.
On the same day, the petitioner's father took her to Gorakhpur and tried to get her admitted but due to the ongoing Covid-19, he failed to get admission in any hospital in Gorakhpur.

Thereafter, finally her father brought her to Delhi and got her admitted in St.
Stephen's Hospital, Delhi.
An FIR bearing no.323/2021, U/s.279/337/338 IPC, PS Dhanghata, Distt. Sant Kabir Nagar, U.P. has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The DAR was treated as a claim petition.
Respondent is the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle.

EVIDENCE 3.
In support of claim, one witness namely Arvind Kumar Rai (Father of minor injured) was examined in petitioner's evidence as PW-1.
PW-1 filed an affidavit Ex.PW1/A wherein he described the occurrence of incident in line with the facts mentioned in Para 1 of this award.
He stated that petitioner was about 07 years of age at the time of accident.
He stated that an expenditure of around Rs.5-6 lacs had been incurred due to this treatment.
He stated that later on it was found that the vehicle involved in the accident was TVS Sport KLS bearing registration no. UP-53DY-6512.

He stated that at the time of accident, the petitioner PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.10.09 13:56:06 +0530 was studying in Delhi and at present the petitioner is residing in Delhi at the given address.
He stated that he incurred Rs.30,000/- on conveyance, Rs.50,000/- on attendant charges, Rs.50,000/- on special diet.
He stated that the injured is entitled to get the relief of compensation of claim/award amounting to Rs.10,00,000/- on account of grievous injuries sustained in the accident.
Thereafter, the matter was fixed for final arguments.
ARGUMENTS 4.
Oral submissions were advanced on behalf of petitioner.
5. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the PANKAJ SHARMA Date:
Baby Ayushi Rai (I) (Petition)(Fir No. ... vs Ramashish Vishvakarma on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100990053/
4 SHARMA 2024.10.09 13:56:09 +0530 accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non- pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating her is also not to reward her or to make her rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd.,
AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited,
(2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
